title: Along which line was the punched paper folded?
description: Holes were punched in a folded square sheet, and the sheet was opened. Each pair of matching holes shows where the fold line must have been, and four holes from a single punch need two folds.
teaching_notes: One idea: the fold line sits halfway between each pair of matching holes, at a right angle to the line joining them. Watch for students who draw the fold through the holes.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (section 9.1, Ruhee block)
video_script.why: The child works backwards from the holes to the fold: matching holes are mirror pictures, so the fold line is halfway between them at a right angle to the line joining them.
video_script.substitution: Imagine folding the opened sheet so that each hole lands exactly on its partner; the crease is the fold line.
video_script.anchor: a hole punch beside four opened square sheets, each with its holes
video_script.payoff_line: The fold line sits halfway between a pair of holes

final_answer.value: first sheet: vertical, through the middle; second: the diagonal from bottom left to top right; third: horizontal, through the middle; last: vertical then horizontal, one hole through all four layers
final_answer.spoken: the first sheet was folded vertically, the second along the diagonal, the third horizontally, and the last vertically and then horizontally

names.Ruhee: activity: punch holes in folded paper to create symmetric patterns

never_show: a fold line drawn through a hole
maths_rules: A hole and its partner are mirror pictures, so the fold line is the line of symmetry between them
The fold line is halfway between the two holes and at a right angle to the line joining them
Two holes left and right at the same height: the line joining them is horizontal, so the fold is vertical, through the middle
Two holes close together near the top right corner: the fold is the diagonal from bottom left to top right, between the two holes
Two holes on the right edge, one above the other: the line joining them is vertical, so the fold is horizontal, through the middle
One fold gives 2 layers and 2 holes; 2 folds give 2 x 2 = 4 layers and 4 holes
Four holes from a single punch: fold vertically, then horizontally (or the other way round); the one hole goes through 4 layers
Check: folding the opened sheet along the line puts each hole on its partner
video_script.design: One idea: the fold line is the line of symmetry between matching holes. Assumes the child knows that a fold makes a mirror picture. Wrong idea: the fold passes through the holes. The sheets stay on the board all video.

<bookmark mark='c'/>In the third sheet, one hole is above the other. The fold is horizontal, halfway between them.

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step four, look at the last sheet. One fold gives two layers, so one punch makes two holes. Two folds give four layers.
<bookmark mark='fold1'/>Fold the square down its vertical middle line.
<bookmark mark='fold2'/>Then fold it again along the horizontal middle line. The sheet becomes a small square.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Punch one hole near the corner that was a corner of the sheet. Opened out, it gives four holes.
